title: Modification of the EPA method 1631E for the quantification of total mercury in natural waters
author: Tassone, Moretti, et al.

steps.title: Prepare 0.5% v/v BrCl solution
steps.instruction: Make a fresh batch of bromine chloride (BrCl) at 0.5% v/v following the previously described salt‑treatment protocol.

substeps.instruction: Treat the required salts according to the earlier suggested procedure.
Dilute the treated mixture to obtain a 0.5% v/v BrCl solution.

steps.title: Calibrate instrument for THg
steps.instruction: Calibrate the mercury analyzer for total mercury (THg) over the range 0.5–100 ng L⁻¹ using working standards prepared from the stock solution.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a series of working standards by diluting the mercury stock solution to concentrations spanning 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 50 and 100 ng L⁻¹ (or any suitable set covering the range).
Run the calibration sequence on the instrument according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Prepare five replicate samples
steps.instruction: Create five separate replicates by diluting the standard water sample so that the resulting signal falls within the linear dynamic range of the method.

substeps.instruction: Determine the dilution factor that places the sample signal inside the calibrated range.
Aliquot the diluted sample into five separate containers.

steps.title: Spike replicates with BrCl and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 0.5% v/v BrCl to each diluted replicate and let the spiked samples stand overnight under a fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Add the appropriate volume of the 0.5% v/v BrCl solution to each replicate to achieve the desired final BrCl concentration.
Cover the containers and leave them overnight (≈12 h) in a fume hood.

steps.title: Analyze replicates and average results
steps.instruction: Measure each replicate with the calibrated instrument, record the THg concentrations, and calculate the mean value.

substeps.instruction: Run each of the five spiked replicates on the instrument.
Document the THg concentration obtained for each replicate.
Compute the arithmetic average of the five measurements.
